reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.text: I have only tried the app once so far to test it for my own patients (I am a psychologist). I found the AI to be supportive and dare I say empathic. It does a good job of building connections between thoughts and emotions, as well as pointing out patterns. It keeps the conversation focused and does not drift. It asks thought provoking questions to help you develop insight and ultimately it helps to develop an action step to apply new insights. I need to play with it a bit more to ensure it is not harmful to vulnerable individuals.

reviews.title: Can Be Toxic
reviews.text:
Not sure what the purpose of this app could ultimately be, as it is surprisingly misleading for a mental health app. I’m shocked to see some of the reviews here. 

When I wanted to journal through some situations to prep for therapy, it would interrupt the thought flow by asking if I was safe, even if I was simply talking about boundaries. This leads to repetition of hurtful moments and a sort of copy and pasting “I’m safe,” at the ends of everything just to progress through a thought. 

To make matters worse, when you ask for tips for coping with situations, it defaults to unhealthy avoidance. If you then attempt to just use the app to self soothe and not dive into deeper topics, it asks you to tell it more. This all left me wondering, what can you actually do with this app to improve any mental health outcomes?
